Abstinence

AB-stih-nents -- stress on the first syllable, AB. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Abstinence is self-restraint from an indulgence; the practice of going without something.

Her month of abstinence from social media left her calmer, better rested, and surprised by how much free time she had.

Worked Example

For the forty days before the festival, the villagers give up sweets entirely, not touching so much as a spoonful of sugar.

That sustained, deliberate practice of going without an indulgence is abstinence. It is not a single moment of saying no -- it is the ongoing state of self-denial, kept up day after day.

How Abstinence Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

self-restraint

self-restraint: control over one's own desires or impulses

temperance

temperance: deliberate moderation or total avoidance of an indulgence

forbearance

forbearance: patient self-control in holding back

Antonyms

indulgence

indulgence: the act of giving in to a desire or pleasure

excess

excess: too much of something; overindulgence

How Strong Is It? — self-restraint → temperance → abstinence

self-restraint vs. abstinence

self-restraint vs. abstinence: Self-restraint is broader and milder than abstinence -- it can mean holding back just a little or just once, while abstinence means going without the thing completely, usually over a sustained period.

temperance vs. abstinence

temperance vs. abstinence: Temperance is the more formal, old-fashioned word: abstinence names the practice of going without an indulgence, while temperance elevates that practice into a whole principle or virtue of disciplined living.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — abs-

prefix — abs-: away, away from (Latin)

root — tin-/ten-

root — tin-/ten-: to hold (Latin tenere)

suffix — -ence

suffix — -ence: state or quality of (Latin -entia)

Put it together

Put it together: Abstinence combines Latin abs- ('away from'), tenere ('to hold'), and -ence ('the state of'). It is literally 'the state of holding oneself away' -- the ongoing condition of keeping your distance from an indulgence.

Use the root in a new word: contain

Use the root in a new word: contain: The firefighters worked through the night to contain the blaze before it reached the town.

Root Check

Word Choice

Abstinence is the noun in the word family whose verb is abstain: the verb names the act of holding back, while abstinence names the ongoing practice or state. It usually takes 'from' -- 'abstinence from sugar' -- and keeping it up for weeks takes genuine determination.
